title: Senior's toolkit: navigating and shaping types
summary: The IDE moves for finding, renaming and generating type code, and the modern C# features that remove boilerplate.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: navigating and shaping types
steps.body: In a real codebase you read far more types than you write. Experienced developers move through code with a few keys, let the IDE write the boilerplate, and use records and required members instead of hand-written equality and constructors.

toolkit.what: Jump to a type or member's definition, to the classes that implement an interface, or to every place it is used.
flags: go to implementation: from `IPaymentGateway` to the real classes
find all references before you change something
toolkit.example: Cursor on IPaymentGateway.Charge, Ctrl+F12: StripeGateway, FakeGateway

toolkit.what: Open any type, member or file by typing part of its name, instead of clicking through folders.
flags: Go to All: types, members, files
go to a symbol anywhere in the workspace

toolkit.what: Rename a class, property or method everywhere it is used, including other projects, in one safe step. Never use find-and-replace for this.
flags: (Visual Studio) also renames `Order.cs` when you rename the class `Order`
toolkit.example: Cursor on Customer, Ctrl+R Ctrl+R, type Account, Enter

toolkit.what: Let the IDE write type boilerplate for you, correctly.
flags: a constructor from the fields you pick
stubs for every member of the interface
turn a constructor that only stores parameters into `class X(IClock clock)`
turn a public field into a property
toolkit.example: Cursor on `: IShape`, Ctrl+., Implement interface

toolkit.what: A record gets value equality, a readable `ToString()` and non-destructive `with` copies for free. Use it for data that is defined by its values: DTOs, money, coordinates.
flags: compares every property, not the reference
a copy with some properties changed; the original stays the same
the same, as a value type
toolkit.example: var discounted = price with { Amount = price.Amount * 0.9m };

toolkit.cmd: public required string Email { get; init; }
toolkit.what: `required` makes the compiler refuse an object initializer that forgets the property; `init` lets it be set only while the object is created.
flags: error CS9035 if a `new` does not set it
settable in the initializer, read-only afterwards
attribute for a constructor that sets them all
toolkit.example: var user = new User { Email = "ada@example.com", Name = "Ada" };

toolkit.what: A primary constructor: the parameters are in scope in the whole class body, which removes the field-plus-constructor boilerplate of dependency-injected services.
flags: they are not readonly; do not reassign them
on a record, the parameters become public properties instead

steps.prompt: A bug: the same order is shipped twice. The de-duplication uses a `HashSet<Order>`, and logging shows two `Order` objects with the same `Id`, customer and lines both in the set. `Order` is a plain `class` with properties. What is going on?
options: A class compares by reference, so two separate objects with equal values are different keys; make `Order` a record (or key the set by `Id`)
`HashSet` allows duplicates when the set is large
The two orders must differ in a property the log does not show
steps.explain: Without overriding `Equals` and `GetHashCode`, a class uses reference identity. A record generates value equality for you; for entities with an identity, keying by `Id` (`HashSet<int>` or `DistinctBy(o => o.Id)`) is often clearer.
`with` makes a copy and leaves `a` alone. The generated `ToString()` lists the properties, and `==` on a record compares values.

steps.prompt: Match the key to what it does.
pairs: go to the classes that implement it
open any type or member by name

items: Fix a misspelled property name used across three projects
Write stubs for every member of a new interface
Create a constructor that sets four fields
See who still calls the method you want to delete
Check every place that sets `Status` before adding a rule

steps.prompt: Make `Email` impossible to forget when creating a `User`, and impossible to change afterwards.
steps.explain: `required` makes a missing `Email = ...` a compile error (CS9035), and `init` allows setting it only in the object initializer.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before you change a type, press Shift+F12 to see who depends on it; when you rename it, let the IDE do it. Reach for a record whenever a type is just its values, and for `required` when a property must always be set.
